title: Follow the GitHub Flow
summary: GitHub Flow is a lightweight way to work on changes. A focused branch and pull request let people inspect an idea before it joins the main branch.
introduction: GitHub Flow is a lightweight way to work on changes. A focused branch and pull request let people inspect an idea before it joins the main branch. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: GitHub Flow is a lightweight way to work on changes. A focused branch and pull request let people inspect an idea before it joins the main branch.

blocks.code: Create a branch -> make focused commits -> open a pull request -> review and check -> merge when ready
blocks.title: Follow the GitHub Flow

blocks.text: The change has a review stage between writing code and combining it with main. Exact project rules decide who may merge.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a branch name for correcting a search label.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not combine unrelated unfinished features into one small review.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
